prime_two_sewing.calculation: the q transposition has determinant -1 and the signed p transposition also has determinant -1, so their product is +1
prime_two_sewing.consequence: W and its contragredient contribute no ordinary determinant-line phase

phase_transport.determinant: det H_e=1 for every z_e in U(1)
phase_transport.cycle: all relative U(1) holonomies are invisible to ordinary determinant, although the operator transport retains them
phase_transport.classification: the phases survive in H^1(graph;U(1)), not in the determinant character

C4.quarter_turn: F_C^2=-I on an even-dimensional doubled endpoint space and F_C^4=I
C4.determinant: det F_C=1 in the prime-two 8-dimensional realization
C4.Maslov: successive ordered crossing signs alternate even though the total four-step determinant holonomy is trivial
C4.orientation_line: the local sign belongs to a Maslov/Pfaffian/metaplectic line finer than the ordinary determinant line

transition_consequence.if_frames: for reciprocal frame changes L,R made from W and W^(-*)

transition_consequence.meaning: the determinant section can glue trivially while the adjugate and Poisson kernel sheaves still require a nontrivial mate

higher_coherence_warning: The scalar Cech defect eta=1 is automatic for determinant-one sewing and cannot certify the kernel defects a=0 or p=0. This gives an explicit finite example of why the fourth-level scalar wrap forgets the orientation data needed to initialize the next phase.

metaplectic_gate.need: choose the source-derived lift of W to the orientation/Pfaffian line
metaplectic_gate.fourfold: the product of four lifted edge characters must be +1 for a closed C4 object
metaplectic_gate.ambiguity: ordinary determinant cannot distinguish the two possible square-root signs
metaplectic_gate.source: the conormal/Maslov orientation local system, not a post hoc determinant square root, must select the lift

authority_boundary: The displayed W is a candidate finite source boundary sewing and is explicitly not identified with an unexposed independent G4 sewing operator. The determinant calculation is exact for this fixture only.
next_iteration: Assemble the ten-iteration result into a dimension ladder: identify what scalarization forgets at each descent and what opposite-face data must be retained to seed the next phase. State the minimal executable constructor contract for a genuine 4-simplex rather than another metaphorical horn.
iteration_result: Prime-two reciprocal sewing has determinant one, as do all orientation-preserving radial phase transports. Therefore scalar determinant descent erases precisely the phase and Maslov information carried by kernel/cofactor transport. The opposite fifth face must retain an orientation/Pfaffian line in addition to the scalar determinant line if it is to seed the next positive phase.
